text: The captain of the guards was waiting beside the gates.
The songs of the old kingdom were remembered by the child.
A basket of apples sits beneath the stairs.
The sound of footsteps echoes through the halls.
Each of the lanterns casts a pool of light.
The queen, accompanied by her guards, walks into the room.
The wolves near the ruined tower are hungry.
The wolf among the wounded horses is asleep.
One of those ancient trees has fallen.
The end of the winding tunnels is near.
The dragon bone necklace lay on the velvet cushion.
She bought three silver dragon pendants at the market.
The village council meeting lasted until dusk.
A stone bridge guard waved us through.
The castle kitchen door stood open.
He repaired the iron horse shoes by the fire.
The river water level rose overnight.
They carried two wolf skin cloaks into the hall.
The watch tower stairs were narrow.
A moonstone necklace caught the candlelight.
The water is cold, and the fire is warm.
The glass was clear enough to see through.
The iron was cold against her skin.
There is blood on the stones.
She poured wine into the cups.
The snow has covered the path.
There was little light beneath the trees.
The paper was too damp to burn.
“Ain’t nobody seen him,” the ferryman said.
“I reckon we oughta go,” she murmured.
“You was there, weren’t you?” he asked.
“Them apples is mine,” said the child.
“I don’t know nothing about it,” the thief replied.
“We was just passing through,” said the traveler.
“Never seen such a beast afore,” she said.
“I done told you twice,” the cook grumbled.
“Thou art welcome in my hall,” said the king.
“Hast thou seen the stars tonight?” she asked.
“I know not whither he has gone.”
“Thee I shall remember, even beyond death.”
“Dost thou hear the bells?”
“Fear not, for the dawn is nigh.”
“What hast thou brought me, traveler?”
“Mayhap the old tales speak true,” he said.
“Come hither, and behold the sea.”
